items.title: Verifica finale (capstone): progetto multi-servizio, prova di manualità e prova di troubleshooting
items.notes: Struttura fedele a GOALS - Verifica: gradini 1-4 crescenti sul progetto, più due prove orali obbligatorie (manualità e troubleshooting) che condizionano il superamento indipendentemente dai gradini raggiunti. Ogni gruppo presenta alla lavagna il proprio progetto (avviato dalla sessione 7), un membro per volta, mentre il docente interroga; i gruppi sono gruppi di lavoro studente, non lane per persona, quindi delivery_pattern resta 'shared'.

criteria: Gradino 1: funzionamento minimo, senza persistenza dei dati
Gradino 2: funzionamento con persistenza (es. database + volume, i dati sopravvivono al riavvio)
Gradino 3: funzionamento con servizi aggiuntivi (es. mock SMTP)
Gradino 4: funzionamento con più repliche di un servizio
Prova di manualità (obbligatoria, gate pass/fail): lo studente modifica live il proprio progetto su richiesta, dimostrando comprensione reale e non copia di un tutorial
Prova di troubleshooting (obbligatoria, gate pass/fail, aggiuntiva e non sostitutiva rispetto alla manualità): lo studente formula ipotesi plausibili su un malfunzionamento teorico dato
rubric.pass_threshold: Superamento di entrambe le prove obbligatorie (manualità e troubleshooting) è condizione necessaria; il voto (18-30) è determinato dal gradino di progetto raggiunto combinato con l'esito delle prove orali, come da GOALS - Verifica.

homework: Completare e consolidare il progetto multi-servizio iniziato in sessione 7, in preparazione alla presentazione finale.

design_decisions.description: reference/curriculum.schema.json (both the plain and the jinja-template copy) has a broken $defs.item: 'delivery_pattern' is listed in required but never defined in properties, while additionalProperties is false at every level; $defs.coverage is referenced from the top level but never defined; $defs.assessment_kind is defined but never referenced from $defs.item.properties. As written, no document can validate against this schema (every item both requires and forbids delivery_pattern; sessions require minItems 1). This file was written by following the task's explicit field list (delivery_pattern, support_material, rubric, covers_node_refs, assessment_kind, design_decisions, coverage, homework) rather than the literal schema text, since the schema cannot be satisfied as written. No mechanical schema validation was run (no Bash/Glob tool available in this session); this needs a human fix to the schema file before any tool-based validation is possible.

STUDENT_PERSONAS/DESIGN flag a concrete mechanism for optional deepening for the 'studente esperto' persona (P-EXP) as 'awaiting: instructional-designer'. This curriculum defaults every item's delivery_pattern to 'shared' — no item uses multi_lane or persona_led, since group work within an activity is student small-group work, not a per-persona lane. BSL-DOCKER-PRIOR, BSL-TECH-ENGLISH and BSL-TERMINAL-COMFORT (held only by P-EXP) are therefore left untaught but also without a defined enrichment path — a human instructional-design decision is still needed here.

Sequence 1 (session 1) is typed item_type 'lesson' with node_ref 'BSL-SHELL' and style 'prerequisite_assessment_quiz', even though BSL-SHELL is listed in coverage.untaught_baseline_node_refs, not taught_node_refs. This is a deliberate choice, not a schema requirement (the schema's 'item' properties do not actually list node_ref as required, only its description says lesson/checkpoint items carry one): a Baseline id was used as node_ref because the item checks that Baseline, and no other item_type fits a prerequisite check. Checking a node is not the same as teaching it; coverage.taught_node_refs intentionally excludes it.

Per-session 'homework' entries (sessions 1-8) total roughly 800-960 minutes across the course, comfortably under the 1200-minute (20-hour) extra-aula cap stated in LOGISTICS. Session-8 homework is empty at the module level but the session already carries the pre-capstone consolidation task.

PRQ-SECURITY-EQ4 is a root node in DESIGN with explicitly undecided depth/content (GOALS EQ_4, tag awaiting instructional-designer). This curriculum allocates a minimal 20-minute placeholder lecture (session 8, sequence 43) so the node is sequenced and DR-TROUBLESHOOTING's dependency is respected, but the actual content is not invented and needs confirmation.

PRQ-SERVICE-REPLICAS is flagged in DESIGN as a coverage gap: it exists only to support tier 4 of the final verification ('funzionamento con più repliche') and is not traceable to any GOAL_00x. Kept in the sequence (session 7, sequence 38) per the DESIGN edges, but flagged here for human confirmation before finalizing session 7 material.

Between DR-IMAGE-DISTRIBUTE (3 new prerequisite nodes) and DR-NETWORK (4 new prerequisite nodes), image distribution was sequenced first per the 'quickest path to a DesiredResult' priority. The overall DR order chosen is LIFECYCLE -> VOLUME -> IMAGE-BUILD -> IMAGE-DISTRIBUTE -> NETWORK -> COMPOSE -> COMPLEX-SYSTEM -> TROUBLESHOOTING.

LOGISTICS requires explicit in-class time for installing Docker in the first lesson, but no DESIGN node models this operational task. It is absorbed into the duration of the PRQ-CLI-DOCKER item (session 1, sequence 6, extended to 70 minutes) rather than added as a node-ref-less item, since the schema requires a node_ref for item_type 'lesson'.

DR-TROUBLESHOOTING has both a mid-course formative practical_pass_fail check (session 8, sequence 44) and the mandatory oral troubleshooting gate embedded in the capstone rubric (sequence 46), per GOALS which states this oral test happens 'sempre in sede di interrogazione' and is mandatory to pass. The two are not redundant: the mid-course one is formative practice, the capstone one is the graded mandatory gate.

DR-COMPLEX-SYSTEM (session 7, sequence 39) was assigned style 'project' rather than 'hands_on', since it integrates multiple already-taught skills (topology design, replicas, compose, volumes, networking) with more than one valid solution path, matching the 'project' definition more closely than a single scripted exercise. Flagged for human confirmation given the borderline nature called out in the task instructions.
